Modified assessment using SLOOS insights:
- The FOMC statement is cautious: modest growth, robust labor markets, elevated inflation, and continued policy restraint (5–5.25% funds rate, ongoing QT), with explicit acknowledgment that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation.
- April 2023 SLOOS corroborates and amplifies the downside growth risks. Banks broadly tightened standards and terms on C&I and commercial real estate loans (wider spreads, lower LTVs, higher DSC requirements), and on multiple consumer categories; loan demand weakened. Reported reasons include a deteriorating economic outlook, higher funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity concerns, and collateral values. Banks expect further tightening, with mid-sized and foreign banks also contributing, and CRE (nonfarm nonresidential and multifamily) a notable vulnerability.
- These SLOOS findings strengthen the likelihood that credit supply constraints will reinforce the drag on business investment and hiring, consistent with the FOMC’s risk language. At the same time, the Fed’s commitment to the 2% objective and systematic implementation should help anchor expectations and support gradual disinflation.

Net tone: more negative on growth than the statement alone, with a constructive path for inflation cooling. sentiment score = -0.30
